reason: E1 supports the premise that limited atomic mobility in solid-precursor synthesis promotes nanoscale compositional fluctuations, but none of the cited evidence addresses melting point depression, local premelting, heterogeneous melting, or the contrast with binary alloys. The key mechanistic premises about melting behavior are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Limited atomic mobility in the solid precursor leads to nanoscale compositional fluctuations and lattice strains
These nanoscale inhomogeneities lower the local melting points
Local premelting occurs at temperatures below the bulk melting point due to these inhomogeneities
The melting process is gradual and heterogeneous, with isolated liquid domains coalescing
This behavior contrasts with the abrupt melting of simpler binary alloy nanoparticles
